content.title: About
content.content: Pasta is a product made from wheat flour and water (sometimes eggs) that is shaped and then boiled in salted water until tender. Cooked pasta serves as a base for countless dishes, from simple sauces to elaborate casseroles.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The earliest references to pasta date back to ancient Rome, but its modern form was refined in Italy during the Middle Ages.
There are more than 600 shapes of pasta, each designed to pair best with specific sauces.
Traditional Italian pasta is made from durum wheat, a hard wheat that gives it a firm structure and helps it hold its shape during cooking.
In Japan, soba (buckwheat noodles) is popular, while rice noodles dominate Chinese cuisine.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Pasta provides a steady release of energy, helping to maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2 and B3 support carbohydrate metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are important for blood formation and normal muscle function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Cooked pasta contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Versatile pairing
items.content: It can be combined with vegetables, legumes, seafood, or lean meats to create a balanced meal.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Pasta contains gluten, so people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should choose gluten‑free alternatives.

items.title: Undercooking
items.content: Undercooked pasta can be hard to digest and cause gastrointestinal discomfort.

items.title: Salt content
items.content: Boiling water is often heavily salted; excessive sodium intake may raise blood pressure.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook pasta in salted water until al dente, then drain. Serve it with tomato, cream, pesto sauces, add it to soups, casseroles, or salads. For a lighter option, choose whole‑grain or legume‑based pasta.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry pasta in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Cooked pasta, cooled to room temperature, should be kept in the refrigerator for no more than 3‑4 days in a sealed container.
